packages.title: No 3D character models inside houses (PS1)
packages.brief:
Owner: inside any house (the player's own or one being visited) nobody is drawn as a 3D model; this is to save PS1 memory.
Today only the PS1 draws a 3D figure in the house: the player's chibi, ps1/src/model.c (model_player_draw), called from ps1/src/room.c (around lines 1661-1801, and the g_model_hold backdrop path near line 2640). Residents are camera-facing billboards already. The GBA and the Dreamcast draw no character models in the house.
Do:
1. ps1/src/room.c draws the player as a billboard like every other actor in the room (same sorting, shadow, light, resting pose and walk frames as a resident; nothing else about the house changes). Check every house mode: Build, Live, Photo, Score, Defend, a visit, HomeMart, and the kept-backdrop path.
2. With the house no longer calling it, model.c (and whatever of prims.c only it uses) is needed only by the first-person / third-person 3D view (ps1/src/view3d.c is the other caller): move it out of resident memory into the 3D / combat overlay group (ps1/tools/ovl_plan.py; docs/PS1.md explains the groups and the slot) if that group has the room, and remove what is dead. Report the resident bytes freed (the "below the stack top" margin before and after, with the boot FMV linked).
3. Combat and levels in third person still show the player model exactly as before (prove with the existing PS1 scripts and screenshots: fast_cellar_tp and the combat perf scripts), and their fps does not drop.
4. This is a visible change the owner asked for: before / after screenshots of the house on the PS1 (home.txt and the room tests) in the evidence directory, docs/PS1.md (the house section and the RAM ledger) updated, a Done line in ROADMAP.md, and the house fps on the PS1 measured before and after (it must stay at 30; it should get cheaper).
If a test or golden image expects the 3D player in the house, update it and say so. Native, GBA and Dreamcast must be byte-identical before and after (prove it).
